title: DH-TRNG: A Dynamic Hybrid TRNG with Ultra-High Throughput and Area-Energy Efficiency
problem: Existing true random number generators suffer from low throughput and high area-energy consumption, creating bottlenecks for practical deployment in cryptographic systems. Current TRNG designs cannot simultaneously achieve high performance, small area footprint, and low power consumption.
motivation: True random number generators are mandatory security primitives that establish the root of trust for encryption systems, making efficient and portable TRNGs critical for practical cryptographic deployments.
method: DH-TRNG proposes a dynamic hybrid TRNG circuitry architecture that combines multiple entropy generation mechanisms with runtime source selection. The design dynamically switches between hybrid entropy sources to optimize throughput while minimizing area and power overhead. The architecture is implemented on FPGAs (Xilinx Virtex-6 and Artix-7) and passes NIST and AIS-31 randomness tests without post-processing.
key_novelty: The dynamic hybrid architecture that intelligently switches between entropy sources to achieve ultra-high throughput with minimal area overhead (8 slices) across different FPGA platforms.
contributions: Dynamic hybrid TRNG architecture combining multiple entropy sources with adaptive source switching
Ultra-high throughput implementation: 670 Mbps on Xilinx Virtex-6, 620 Mbps on Artix-7 using only 8 slices
Portable design achieving 2.63× improvement in Throughput/Power ratio over state-of-the-art TRNGs
Statistical validation: passes both NIST and AIS-31 tests without post-processing
limitations: The abstract does not discuss scalability to larger designs, absolute power consumption, or comparison with alternative TRNG approaches beyond FPGA implementations.
primary_theme: high-throughput area-efficient FPGA TRNG with dynamic hybrid architecture
